rem:einstein-ether-substrate:
Remark Einstein's ether and the categorical substrate. Einstein, in his 1920 Leiden address, gave a precise characterisation of the relativistic ether:

"We may assume the existence of an ether; only we must give up ascribing a definite state of motion to it, i.e. we must by abstraction take from it the last mechanical characteristic which Lorentz had still left it. We shall see later that this point of view [...] is justified by the results of the general theory of relativity."

The QOU substrate q_0 is the categorical analogue of this ether-without-mechanical-state. It is a background organisational structure — a deformation parameter that encodes the groupoid symmetry of Bring's curve — but it carries no privileged velocity, no Lorentz-violating medium, and no mechanical degrees of freedom. What it does carry is the algebra: the Hecke parameter governing braid-group representations.

Where Lorentz's ether supplied a preferred rest frame (and was therefore excluded by special relativity), the QOU substrate supplies only a preferred algebraic deformation class. The substrate q_0 is fixed not by any physical medium at rest but by the cohomological structure of H^1(\mathrm{Bring}) = 2W — the first cohomology of Bring's surface. It is a categorical, not mechanical, invariant.

This reading is consistent with Einstein's own conclusion: that one may retain an ether so long as one removes the last mechanical characteristic (a definite state of motion). The QOU substrate is a relational invariant — fixed by the global structure of the observable algebra — rather than a local mechanical datum.

conj:higgs-t28:
Conjecture The Higgs boson as T(2,8): the link spanning three exceptional divisors. The Higgs boson is the torus link T(2,8) — the unique genus-3 link on the Bring's surface whose Seifert surface spans all three exceptional divisors simultaneously.

The three exceptional divisors.

The Bring's surface (\chi = -6, genus 4) has three color tubes (r, g, b) (color tube coordinates). The brane tower blow-up produces three exceptional divisors D_r, D_g, D_b, one for each color fiber. The Borromean link \mathcal{B}_3 (Borromean quark) lies at the intersection of these three divisors.

The torus links T(2, 2k) on the Bring's surface have genus k - 1 and interact with the exceptional divisors by genus:

Link Genus Divisors spanned Role
T(2,2) 0 0 (trivial Seifert) Gluon
T(2,4) 1 1 (D_r or D_g or D_b) W boson
T(2,6) 2 2 (D_r \cup D_g etc.) Z boson
T(2,8) 3 all 3 (D_r \cup D_g \cup D_b) Higgs

The torus link T(2,8) is the first and only link with a Seifert surface genus large enough to span all three exceptional divisors. Its genus (3) exactly matches the number of color tubes.

Scalar (spin 0) character of T(2,8).

The two components of T(2,8) each wind 4 times around the torus longitude and 1 time around the meridian. The fermion--boson correspondence (fermion--boson knot--link) identifies even-n links as bosons, with components related by the fiber adjoint involution.

For T(2,8), the linking number is 4. The two components cross each other 8 times, contributing 4 crossings each. The Reeb winding of the two components cancels exactly: one winds +4 and the other -4 around the Reeb direction. The total angular momentum vanishes:

  J =  J_1 + J_2 =  +4 + (-4) =  0.

The torus link T(2,8) is therefore a scalar (spin-0) boson. It is the only member of the T(2,n) family where Reeb windings cancel exactly due to genus-3 symmetry.

The Higgs mechanism as linking with T(2,8).

A particle (knot or link) acquires mass by crossing with T(2,8). The crossing energy (crossing energy) of the interaction is proportional to the number of crossings between the particle and the Higgs link:

  m_{\mathrm{Higgs}}  \propto 
  N_{\mathrm{cross}}(T(2,8))
   \times  \frac{q - q^{-1}}{q + q^{-1}}

where N_{\mathrm{cross}}(L) counts crossings between the particle braid and the link L.

Particles that cross all three exceptional divisors (heavy quarks, W, Z) interact strongly with T(2,8) and acquire large masses. Particles confined to fewer divisors interact less. The photon (\mathbf{1}_{B_4}, the 4-strand identity, knot-trivial under Markov closure; see confined-particle) has zero crossings with T(2, 8) and remains massless.

Mass of the Higgs.

The torus link T(2,8) has genus 3. Its Seifert surface area is proportional to the product of the three exceptional divisor volumes. The self-crossing energy of T(2,8) determines its mass (\sim 125 GeV) via the Skein polynomial evaluated at q = q_0:

  m_H =  \frac{\mathrm{Vol}(\text{Seifert}(T(2,8)))}{\hbar_q^2}
  \cdot c_{\mathcal{B}}

Here c_{\mathcal{B}} is the historical common-scale factor of the Borromean baryon mass formula (the purged \lambda_{\mathrm{scale}} literal, since re-expressed there as the common Borromean term \mathfrak{m}_{\mathcal{B}_3}(q_0)). It is recorded as a near-form resting on an acknowledged calibration input. The canonical production mass shape absorbs it into the per-block density, m = m_e\,\mathrm{Vol}(K)\,\varrho(K)/\hbar_q^2 (no standalone scale factor). This \sim 125 GeV heuristic estimate remains exploratory, conditional on that open closure.

The Higgs mass stems from the genus-3 Seifert surface volume, determined by the three color tube volumes of the Bring's surface. In the 2-strand torus-link Plancherel trace hierarchy P_m(h) = \sum_{j=0}^m \tfrac{1}{2}\binom{m+j}{2j}h^{2j} (h = q - q^{-1}, with (q+q^{-1})\cdot 2P_m(h) = q^{2m+1}+q^{-(2m+1)} a proved identity), dressing the W \to Z step by ([2]_q/2)^2 = 1 + h^2/4 reconciles the W-anchored and Z-anchored categorical mass ratios:

  m_H^{(W)} \;=\; m_W\,\frac{P_4(h_0)}{P_2(h_0)}\,\frac{6}{5}\,\frac{[2]_{q_0}}{2}\,C_{\mathrm{loop}},
  \qquad
  m_H^{(Z)} \;=\; m_Z\,\frac{P_4(h_0)}{P_3(h_0)}\,\frac{6}{5}\,\frac{2}{[2]_{q_0}}\,C_{\mathrm{loop}},

so the W-anchor and Z-anchor evaluations agree to within 21.9\;\mathrm{MeV} (174.7\;\mathrm{ppm}) and land inside the PDG 125.20 \pm 0.11\;\mathrm{GeV} window under the parameter-free 1-loop / Bring zero-mode factors (125.230\;\mathrm{GeV} from W and 125.208\;\mathrm{GeV} from Z with C_{\mathrm{loop}} = 1 - \tfrac{2}{3\pi}\hbar_q^2; 125.200\;\mathrm{GeV} from W and 125.178\;\mathrm{GeV} from Z with C_{\mathrm{loop}} = 1 - \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}}/\pi; or 125.052\;\mathrm{GeV} / 125.030\;\mathrm{GeV} with C_{\mathrm{loop}} = 1 - 2G h_0^4). Which 1-loop factor is canonical remains open alongside the C1/C_{\text{sector}} torus-link identification.

Uniqueness of the Higgs.

On the genus-4 Bring's surface, the Seifert surface of T(2,8) has genus 3, filling 3 of the 4 available handles. Up to isotopy, there is exactly one way to embed a genus-3 surface into a genus-4 surface leaving one handle free. The next link T(2,10) would require genus 4 (all handles), saturating the surface and precluding the coexistence of Borromean and knot structures. Therefore, T(2,8) is the unique Higgs candidate.
prop:s5-equivariant-torus-knots:
Proposition S_5-equivariant torus-knot embeddings: the \mathbb{Z}_s and monodromy tests. Let \Sigma be a Riemann surface with automorphism group \mathrm{Aut}(\Sigma) = S_5 (Bring's surface). A torus knot T_{2, s} with s \geq 3 coprime to 2 admits an equivariant embedding into \Sigma if and only if

  s  \in  \{3,\, 5\}.

An equivariant embedding preserves the intrinsic cyclic symmetry \mathbb{Z}_s of the knot.

Two tests. The fibration of T_{2,s} has monodromy of order 2s. For odd s the monodromy group is \mathbb{Z}_{2s} \cong \mathbb{Z}_2 \times \mathbb{Z}_s, the two rotations of the torus knot taken together. The criterion above is the \mathbb{Z}_s test: it asks only that the \mathbb{Z}_s rotation be realised in S_5. The stronger monodromy test asks that the whole \mathbb{Z}_{2s} be realised, that is, that S_5 contain an element of order 2s. This holds if and only if

  s = 3.

Under the monodromy test only T_{2,3} passes; T_{2,5} fails because S_5 has no element of order 10. The \mathbb{Z}_s test is the weaker of the two, and a statement that a knot is S_5-equivariant should say which test it uses.

prf:s5-equivariant-torus-knots:
Proof Proof of s5 equivariant torus knots. An equivariant embedding requires \mathbb{Z}_s \hookrightarrow \mathrm{Aut}(\Sigma) = S_5. The cyclic symmetry of the knot must match a symmetry of the ambient surface. An injection \mathbb{Z}_s \hookrightarrow S_5 exists if and only if S_5 contains an element of order s. The orders of elements in S_5 are the least common multiples of the parts of integer partitions of 5.

See Table.

The realised orders in S_5 are \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6\}. The condition \gcd(2, s) = 1 forces odd s \geq 3. This restricts the possible orders to \{3, 5\}. \square

The monodromy test. An element of order 2s with s odd and s \geq 3 must have order 6, 10 or 30 among the divisors of 60. An element whose order is divisible by 5 is a 5-cycle, of order exactly 5, so orders 10 and 30 do not occur. Order 6 is realised by a transposition times a disjoint 3-cycle. Hence the monodromy test holds only for s = 3. \square

Corollary. Among torus knots T_{2, s} with s \geq 3, exactly two admit cyclic-symmetry-preserving embeddings into \Sigma_4 (Bring's surface): T_{2, 3} and T_{2, 5}. Any other torus knot of this family either breaks the symmetry in the embedding or fails to embed topologically (Seifert genus > 4, or s \geq 11).

Comparison with genus-based embedding. Pure topological (Seifert-genus) embedding into \Sigma_4 admits four knots: T_{2, 3}, T_{2, 5}, T_{2, 7}, and T_{2, 9}. The stronger equivariant criterion retains only T_{2, 3} and T_{2, 5}. The knots T_{2, 7} and T_{2, 9} are topologically admissible but symmetry-broken.
rem:symmetry-preserving-leptons:
Remark Symmetry-preserving versus symmetry-broken lepton generators. The classification of prop:s5-equivariant-torus-knots admits a sharp physical reading. The three charged lepton generations map to torus knots:

  \text{electron} \;=\; T_{2,3},
  \qquad
  \text{muon} \;=\; T_{2,5},
  \qquad
  \text{tau} \;=\; T_{2,7}.

Under pure topological embedding (Seifert genus \leq 4), all three fit on Bring's surface. Under the stronger equivariant criterion—preserving the knot's intrinsic cyclic symmetry along the embedding—the proposition cuts the list to two:

Particle Knot Cyclic symmetry \mathbb{Z}_s \hookrightarrow S_5? Embedding
electron T_{2,3} \mathbb{Z}_3 yes (3-cycle) symmetry-preserving
muon T_{2,5} \mathbb{Z}_5 yes (5-cycle) symmetry-preserving
tau T_{2,7} \mathbb{Z}_7 no (no order-7 element in S_5) symmetry-broken
(ghost) T_{2,9} \mathbb{Z}_9 no (no order-9 element) symmetry-broken, saturates g=4
(ghost) T_{2,11} \mathbb{Z}_{11} no doubly excluded (g = 5 > 4)

Reading. The electron and muon are the only leptons whose cyclic rotational symmetry is realized by a genuine element of \mathrm{Aut}(\Sigma_4) = S_5. The tau embeds topologically by virtue of its genus (g(T_{2,7}) = 3 \leq 4) but fails equivariance: its \mathbb{Z}_7 symmetry is not a subgroup of S_5. The tau is a lepton in the topological spectrum, but not in the symmetry spectrum.

Physical consequence. If lepton-generation structure derives from the cyclic symmetry of a \Sigma_4-embedded torus knot, the equivariant criterion predicts exactly two generations of charged leptons. Three generations are observed, matching the topological-embedding criterion. The equivariant proposition sharpens this: tau carries its mass because the symmetry-broken embedding still admits a Seifert surface, not because an S_5-compatible cyclic structure exists. sec:double-slit-intro:
Double-slit interferometry provides a direct experimental probe of the q-deformed propagation law. A complete quantum description must account simultaneously for the fine interference fringes, the macroscopic diffraction envelope, and the loss of phase coherence under path detection. On the categorical substrate, the diffraction pattern separates into two distinct propagation regimes according to whether the incident state carries hyperbolic volume:

  1. Massive particles (trefoil and hyperbolic closures): A massive fermion propagates via the full q-Laplacian (Particle (q-harmonic form)), whose cross-coupling terms mix spatial translation with the internal Reeb fibre to produce a q-deformed \mathrm{sinc}^2 diffraction envelope.
  2. Photons (exceptional-divisor flux modes): A photon is a volumeless excitation on the exceptional divisor (Exceptional divisor at p) carrying the two-strand Hecke colour content \gamma = \mathbf{1} + \varphi_0\sigma_0 + \varphi_1\sigma_1 + \varphi_{01}\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1} (Color content as formal linear combination in H_3(q)), where \sigma_0, \sigma_1 encode transverse polarization and generate a self-similar Julia-set envelope measure \mu_J.

In the classical limit q \to 1, both envelopes collapse to standard Fraunhofer diffraction. For massive electrons in exterior vacuum (q_{\mathrm{local}}(y) \to 1 outside the femtometre-scale slit-wall boundary layers), the aperture-averaged prediction coincides with Fraunhofer diffraction to parts per million and reproduces the central five-order modulation of the 600\;\mathrm{eV} single-electron diffraction dataset of Roger Bach, Damian Pope, Sy-Hwang Liou, and Herman Batelaan [bach2013], whereas a hypothetical uniform vacuum q = q_0 \approx 1.1100 would broaden the fringe spacing by +11.00\% and the Hodge diffraction envelope by +23.21\%.
def:double-slit-q-phase:
Definition q-deformed path phase. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with substrate parameter q \in k^{\times} (substrate parameter), and let \gamma_i (i = 1,2) be two paths through slits of width a separated by distance d.

For a massive excitation of rest mass m, the spatial wavelength is not an external optical parameter; it is forced by Lorentz covariance of the internal meridian clock. In its rest frame, the excitation ticks at the Compton angular frequency \omega_0 = m c^2 / \hbar of the exceptional-divisor meridian cycle (meridian Compton tick). Following Louis de Broglie (1924), boosting along the beam axis at velocity v with Lorentz factor \gamma^2(1 - v^2 / c^2) = 1 transforms proper time as \tau_{\mathrm{prop}} = \gamma(t - v x / c^2) and decomposes the invariant clock phase into temporal and spatial components:

  \omega_0 \tau_{\mathrm{prop}}
  = \frac{E t - p x}{\hbar},
  \qquad
  E = \gamma m c^2,
  \qquad
  p = \gamma m v,
  \qquad
  E^2 - (p c)^2 = (m c^2)^2.

The spatial gradient fixes the relativistic de Broglie wavenumber k_{\mathrm{dB}} = p / \hbar and wavelength \lambda_{\mathrm{dB}} = 2\pi\hbar / p = h / (\gamma m v), with phase velocity E / p satisfying (E / p)\,v = c^2.

Along each slit trajectory \gamma_i, the q-exterior derivative d_q = q^{-1}d + (1 - q^{-1})\pi_V \circ d splits the accumulated q-deformed path phase into horizontal and vertical parts:

  \Phi_q^{(i)}(y)
  = \frac{1}{\hbar_q}\!\int_{\gamma_i}\! d_q\psi
  = q^{-1}\Phi_{\mathrm{geom}}^{(i)}(y)
      + (1 - q^{-1})\Phi_{\mathrm{Reeb}}^{(i)}(y),

where:

  • \Phi_{\mathrm{geom}}^{(i)}(y) = (2\pi / \lambda_{\mathrm{dB}})\,\ell_i(y) is the horizontal de Broglie geometric phase along path length \ell_i(y),
  • \Phi_{\mathrm{Reeb}}^{(i)}(y) = \int_{\gamma_i} \iota_\xi\varTheta is the vertical Reeb phase, and
  • \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1} is the quantum Planck constant.

Subtracting the two paths at scattering angle \theta gives the q-deformed interference phase difference

  \Delta\Phi_q(y)
  = \Phi_q^{(1)}(y) - \Phi_q^{(2)}(y)
  = q^{-1}\frac{2\pi d\sin\theta}{\lambda_{\mathrm{dB}}}
      + (1 - q^{-1})\Delta\phi_\xi(y)
  = \frac{2\pi d\sin\theta}{\lambda_q}
      + (1 - q^{-1})\Delta\phi_\xi(y),

where \Delta\phi_\xi(y) is the Reeb phase mismatch and \lambda_q = q\lambda_{\mathrm{dB}} is the stretched effective fringe wavelength. At detector distance L, the horizontal q^{-1} factor stretches the Young fringe spacing to \Delta y_q = q\lambda_{\mathrm{dB}} L / d, whereas the q^{-2}\Delta classical Hodge core of the q-Laplacian expansion broadens the single-slit diffraction envelope by q^2 for controlled comparison with relativistic 600\;\mathrm{eV} electron interferometry [bach2013]. At q = 1, the Reeb mismatch vanishes and \lambda_q reduces to \lambda_{\mathrm{dB}}.
prop:double-slit-massive-pattern:
Proposition Massive-particle interference pattern. Let \alpha be a massive q-harmonic form (particle) incident on a double slit. The q-deformed intensity at scattering angle \theta is

  I_q(\theta)
  =  4I_0\cos^2\!\!\left(\frac{\Delta\Phi_q(\theta)}{2}\right)
        \cdot
        \left(\frac{\sin\beta_q(\theta)}{\beta_q(\theta)}\right)^{\!2}.

The interference phase is

  \Delta\Phi_q(\theta)
  =  q^{-1}\frac{2\pi d\sin\theta}{\lambda}
        +  (1 - q^{-1})\Delta\phi_\xi(\theta).

The envelope parameter is

  \beta_q(\theta)
  =  q^{-1}\frac{\pi a\sin\theta}{\lambda}
        +  (1 - q^{-1})^2\beta_\xi(\theta).

The term \beta_\xi(\theta) is the spin-core contribution of the q-Laplacian expansion.

The q-Laplacian separates into three scales:

  • Classical core (\propto q^{-2}): Standard Hodge diffusion \Delta.
  • Spin core (\propto (1 - q^{-1})^2): Pure Reeb dynamics \Delta_\xi.
  • Cross-coupling (\propto q^{-1}(1 - q^{-1})): Mixes spatial and Reeb modes.

The fringe spacing is

  \Delta y_q =  \frac{q\lambda L}{d}.

The envelope half-width broadens:

  w_q =  \frac{q^2\lambda L}{a}
        \left(1 +  (1 - q^{-1})^2
        \frac{\langle\Delta_\xi\rangle}{\langle\Delta\rangle}\right).

At q = 1, this recovers the classical Fraunhofer pattern. In the 600\;\mathrm{eV} single-electron double-slit buildup experiment of Roger Bach, Damian Pope, Sy-Hwang Liou, and Herman Batelaan [bach2013] (a = 50\;\mathrm{nm}, d = 280\;\mathrm{nm}, relativistic \lambda_{\mathrm{dB}} \approx 50.05\;\mathrm{pm}, 6{,}235 electrons across the central five interference orders), an electrostatic quadrupole lens magnifies the pattern without an independent angular scale bar, making the dimensionless envelope-to-fringe ratio w_q / \Delta y_q \ge q(d/a) and the order-m peak modulation I_q(\theta_m)/I_q(0) = \mathrm{sinc}^2(m\pi a / (q d)) the magnification-invariant observables. Under the local vacuum profile q_{\mathrm{local}}(y) \to 1, the aperture-averaged departure \langle q_{\mathrm{local}} - 1 \rangle_a \le 1.70 \times 10^{-6} across a = 50\;\mathrm{nm} agrees with q = 1 Fraunhofer to better than 8.1 \times 10^{-6} pointwise and predicts I(\theta_{\pm 2})/I(0) = \mathrm{sinc}^2(5\pi/14) \approx 0.6448 against the digitized Figure 3e mean m = \pm 2 peak height 0.6552 (1.58\% difference), whereas a uniform exterior q = q_0 \approx 1.1100 would lift I_{q_0}(\theta_{\pm 2})/I_{q_0}(0) to 0.7026 and stretch the physical fringe spacing \Delta\theta_{q_0} = q_0\lambda_{\mathrm{dB}}/d by +11.00\%.

prf:skein-mass-relation:
Proof Proof of q-Deformed Skein Relation. The electron is the word \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 \in B_3, whose closure is the Hopf link (the trefoil 3_1 is kept as the backup reading). Neither closure has a hyperbolic complement, so the hyperbolic volume is 0 under either reading. The electron sits at the base of the topological tower, providing the unit against which all other masses are measured. The Higgs field is identified with the figure-eight knot 4_1 (cohomological embedding). Its algebraic quantum volume \mathrm{Vol}_q(\beta_{4_1}) τ-realises to the hyperbolic-volume constant \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) \approx 2.02988.

Applying the algebraic topological mass formula (algebraic topological mass) to the muon–electron ratio eliminates the overall mass scale. This gives m_\mu / m_e = \Phi_1(4_1) / \hbar_q^{2} at the \mathbb{Q}(q) level. Here, \Phi_1(4_1) = \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}(\mathrm{Vol}_q(4_1)) is the \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}-image of the algebraic quantum volume (Algebraic quantum volume \mathrm{Vol}_q(K)). Under \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}, the value \Phi_1(4_1) specialises to the numerical hyperbolic volume \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) via the volume conjecture [kashaev1997, murakami-murakami2001]. This constitutes τ-side naming of the algebraic value, not a derivation input. Substituting \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1} and the CODATA value m_\mu / m_e \approx 206.7682827(46) yields

  \hbar_q^{2}
  = \frac{\mathrm{Vol}(4_1)}{m_\mu / m_e}
  = \frac{2.02988}{206.7683}
  \approx 0.009817,
  \qquad
  \hbar_q \approx 0.09908,

so 1/q = 1 - 0.09908 = 0.9009 and q \approx 1.10998.

The Skein relation acts as the mass-functional analogue of the Kauffman bracket recursion. At each crossing in the color-exchange diagram of a hadron, the three resolutions L_+, L_-, and L_0 satisfy q\mathcal{M}(L_+) - q^{-1}\mathcal{M}(L_-) = (q^{1/2}-q^{-1/2})\mathcal{M}(L_0). This relation descends from the q-deformed \mathrm{SU}(2) Chern--Simons functional on the 1-jet bundle prolongation of the CR manifold (Chapter). \square
